deities: Shiva - 525 Shivlings arranged in a Swastika formation
Main Shivalinga: 15-ft, ~16-ton black-stone monolith in Pashupatinath form (carved from a single stone; 1008 small Shivlings on it per one account)
Pashupatinath: four-faced white idol at the Swastika's centre
Ganesha, Goddess Annapurna, Shiva Parivar, a sage's shrine
Kaal Bhairav (guarding the Amrit Sarovar at the entrance)
festivals: Raasleela (celebrated with fervour per visitor accounts)

history.dynasty: No royal dynasty; founded by Naga sadhus of the Juna Akhara
history.period: Late 20th century (1985-2007); one aggregator claims 1949 - conflict flagged, likely wrong
history.summary: Identity verified: the Shivpuri Dham at Thegda (Thekra) on Thekra Canal Road, Kota, is the well-documented Shiva complex with 525 Shivlings arranged in a Swastika-shaped layout. Its origins trace to Naga Baba Rana Rampuri, who laid the foundation in 1985 after arriving in Kota (inspired by a pilgrimage to the Pashupatinath temple in Kathmandu, Nepal); the first 12 Shivlings were installed in 1987, and after his death his disciple Naga Baba Sanatan Puri completed the work - all 525 Shivlings were ceremonially consecrated in 2007 after a grand 111-kund Mahayagya. Local belief: worshipping all 525 Shivlings equals worship of the 12 Jyotirlingas. Holy waters from sacred rivers (including the Sindhu) were brought at establishment. Coordinates from geocoding agree with the site's published location (25.162246, 75.87485).

name: Shivpuri Dham, Kota
town_description: Kota, on the Chambal river in southeastern Rajasthan, is the state's industrial and education (coaching) hub, known for Kota stone, Chambal gardens, the Garadia Mahadev gorge and nearby palaces.

travel.airport: Kota has no commercial airport; Jaipur International Airport (~240-250 km) or Udaipur (verify distances).
travel.railway: Dakaniya Tal station is ~1.3 km from the temple; Kota Junction is ~10 km (verify).
travel.road: Thegda/Thekra area, Thekra Canal Road, Kota - reach by auto-rickshaw or taxi from Kota Junction.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Sawan month and Mahashivratri for the grand celebrations (very crowded).
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily. Food stalls, parking and washrooms available nearby; the complex has trees, peacocks and a pond.
